summary: Six instruments must be rebuilt. Round 3's headline finding — that cadence and competence read r.frame while every shipped trace numbers frames f — was real and important, and the round fixed those two without asking how many siblings there were. There are two more, both in tools R1 and R2 both accepted, and one of them does not merely mis-stamp a beat: it promotes a hedged confidence-0.7 verdict to confidence 1.0 and cites corroborating evidence the trace does not support. Separately, build-viability's three-anchor model detector — the round's cleverest work — silently MIS-DETECTS: an injected one-line half-wire that leaves all three anchors matched produces byte-identical tool output while the running engine goes from six distinct race-dependent disposition-clause sets to one race-invariant set, and the flagship --cross-check reports its usual 'AGREES on 240 pairs, 0 disagreements' because every row becomes agrees:null and null is not false.
worst_instrument_why: Third round running. The model detector was built to stop the offer model being hard-coded, and it replaced hard-coding with a heuristic over source text whose three anchors all describe PLUMBING and none of which asks whether _questDispositionModel() applies derivedDisposition(). Demonstrated on a full shadow tree: injecting `if (!this.__raceGatesEnabled) return null;` at the top of the model closure leaves all three anchor regexes matching, and the tool reports model='derived', 504/540 viable and the same 36 dunmer FAILs as the unbroken tree — charging the build 36 false failures — while the engine on that same tree emits zero disposition clauses for every signature. Its --cross-check confirms the mis-detection instead of catching it, and the artifact prints model='derived' next to 'RACE-INVARIANT: 1 distinct disposition-clause set' and exits 0 without reconciling them.
harness_state: node tools/harness/boot-check.mjs PASS before and after every measurement. smoke.mjs never boots the engine and was not used.

The Build status page must not read those thirteen as coverage.

tools.reads_running_world: partly — only under --cross-check, which is opt-in and cannot fail in the direction that matters
findings: MIS-DETECTS. Injected half-wire on shadow tree (model installed, consulted, fed to gate, returns null) leaves 3/3 anchors matched. Tool output byte-identical to unbroken tree: model='derived', 504/540 viable, same 36 dunmer FAILs at speaker-teel-ashaan.

Engine on the same broken tree: 1 distinct disposition-clause set over 6 signatures (RACE-INVARIANT), 0 disposition clauses per signature. Unbroken tree: 6 distinct sets, 3/5/4/1/1/1 clauses. The world changed completely; the instrument did not move.
Correct answer on the broken tree is 540/540 viable (raw 50 clears the 50-bar, confirmed by the engine emitting no clause). The tool charges 36 FALSE FAILs.

--cross-check cannot fail in this direction: rows where the engine reports modelled:false get agrees:null, and only agrees===false is pushed to disagreements. rows.push() still runs, so rows_compared still reports 240. Headline 'AGREES on 240 (signature, giver) pairs; 0 disagreement(s)' printed on a tree where zero rows were resolved.
The artifact holds its own refutation: model='derived' printed alongside cc.race_sensitive=false, unreconciled, exit 0.
None of the three anchors checks that derivedDisposition is CALLED. All three describe plumbing.
A single global model string is the wrong shape: _questDispositionModel returns null per-NPC when reaction_group is absent, so the build's real model is per-giver mixed.
FIXED since R2 and verified: --signatures is now read (accepts 'all', a race id, or a count; an unrecognised value is a usage error).
rebuild: Assert cross_check.race_sensitive === (OFFER_MODEL.model === 'derived') and refuse on disagreement. Three lines; the tool already computes both sides.
Treat agrees:null as unresolved, not agreement. Report rows_resolved/rows_unresolved; make the cross-check unmeasurable when rows_resolved === 0.
Add a fourth anchor on the arithmetic (derivedDisposition is reached inside _questDispositionModel), not on the plumbing.
Better: stop treating the model as a global string; explainDisposition().modelled reports it per-giver, live.
tools.scoring_consequence: RI-CHR01 Distinctness and RI-CHR03 Decidability must not be scored from this run — not because the build lacks the mechanism (the offer path IS genuinely race-sensitive on the real tree, 6 distinct clause sets over 6 signatures, which I confirmed) but because the instrument cannot tell a wired race term from a dead one.

tools.self_test: 8/8 — green because the fixture speaks the tool's private dialect
findings: line 111 reads `const f = r.frame ?? 0` from trace.jsonl, whose every record is keyed `f`. Has never worked on a real trace.

line 244, the self-test's own fixture builder: `const rec = (f, events, extra = {}) => ({ frame: f, … })`. The fixture is written by the same hand that reads it, in a dialect the engine does not speak.

DEMONSTRATED, same events two dialects (topic at frame 0, item at frame 100000 = 27.8 min later, far outside RI-EXP01's 30 s window): `frame` dialect gives f:100000, t_min:27.78, confidence 0.7, via 'previously mentioned', evidence [2]. `f` dialect (the engine's) gives f:0, t_min:0, confidence 1.0, no via, evidence [2,1].

So it is not only that every beat in every real session is stamped at minute zero (and beat-diff compares beat logs by time). `f - t.frame <= 30*fps` becomes `0 - 0 <= 1800`, always true, so the hedged verdict is PROMOTED to a confidence-1.0 direct hit that CITES the topic line as corroboration. The tool manufactures evidence for a window it never checked.

Same constant 0 defeats `Math.abs(qf - a.frame) <= 60*fps` at line 195, so nearStage is always true and the `odd` detector at line 197 can NEVER fire — in a tool whose --self-test advertises 'prove each detector fires on a synthetic positive AND stays silent on a synthetic negative'.
line 115 reads r.player.region and r.world.region; neither is written by any artifact in the 78-artifact census, so the 'release / area change' signature cannot fire either.
rebuild: Read `r.f ?? r.frame`, as competence.frameOf() already does.
Make the self-test fixture emit the engine's dialect, or run both and assert agreement.
Report unmeasurable rather than 0 when no record carries a frame key.
Drop or rename the dead player.region / world.region reads.

referred_judgements.ruling: UPHELD, with two corrections. Not a bar quietly relaxed.
referred_judgements.why: RI-JRN02 §C line 141 bans an equipment UPGRADE and M-I9 asks for IDENTICAL EQUIPMENT. Two-handing a sword is the same sword — a grip chosen and unchosen many times inside one fight, not a shopping trip. A clause that voided on it would return void on every real fight, which is R2's 'cannot pass' failure in a different coat. The builder flagged it rather than burying it, which is what rule 3 wants.
corrections: As reported the flag is close to meaningless: stance is sampled at ONE record per encounter window and is a fast-varying per-frame value. Diffing two instants of it is noise. Two-handing IS a real competence confound (damage, moveset, poise), so the honest form is a FRACTION over each window — player.stance is on 78906 records across 20 artifacts, so the trace supports it today.

The item's own remedy is not offered. M-I9 says neither 'void' nor 'proceed' but 're-run E_late with E_first's loadout via loadState'. competence offers neither the re-run nor a note that it is skipping it.
referred_judgements.filed_as_corpus_conflict: loadState is classified load-state and is REFUSED by session-run's first-hour, ending and build-identity profiles. One item prescribes a remedy another item prohibits. Somebody must rule on which wins; it is not the tool builder's call and it should not be settled by silence.

referred_judgements.ruling: THE SCENARIO MUST BE AUTHORED. Declared is not discharged.
referred_judgements.why: F3 is 'boss arena, 1 boss, active fight'; the substitute cmb-duel-infantry is 'player vs one INFANTRY trash enemy on flat ground'. The artifact defends the swap with a bare assertion — 'the property M6 tests is not sensitive to which fight is running' — which is a hypothesis, not a measurement, and the one most likely to be wrong: sim/render coupling surfaces under load and complexity, which a boss arena has and a flat-ground trash duel does not. Substituting the quiet scene is a substitution in the PERMISSIVE direction, and R1 ruled on that shape.
referred_judgements.authorable: Yes. Ten scenario files, a small schema, and the content exists — build-viability's own tier-5 census names a shipped champion cohort, gate-drowned-xanmeer:1xchampion_hist_marked.
referred_judgements.disposition: Author F3 from shipped content and re-run M6 against it at --sim-frames 3600. Until then M6 is corpus_debt charged to CONTENT, not to the tool and not to the builder — the declaration was the right thing to do. A declared substitution renewed every round on a 10-point item is how a bar relaxes without anyone deciding to relax it.

referred_judgements.ruling: A VALID MEASUREMENT, NOT A TAUTOLOGY — with a limit that must be stated.
referred_judgements.why_not_tautology: renders_observed is after.rendersTotal - before.rendersTotal, read from the ENGINE's loop.stats.rendersTotal (core/loop.js:165); if the engine failed to render the counter would say so. The perturbation is genuinely four different things — one render every 1, 2, 4 and infinity fixed steps — a real variation in sim/render interleaving applied through the engine's own engine.js:3212 path. The MEASURED quantity is body_sha256 invariance across those interleavings, which is exactly HF2, and the control is not vacuous: the broken build changes both step count (61 vs 60) and hash.
referred_judgements.limit_that_must_be_declared: Because renderRateHz is two-state on stepFrames, the sweep never exercises the consumer of the rate AS a rate — core/loop.js's rAF loop, which in harness mode neither steps nor draws. M6 as measured covers the INTERLEAVING axis in HARNESS MODE; the shipping render path is not tested at all. The tool says the rAF loop 'neither steps nor draws'; it does not say the consequence, which is that a decoupling defect living in the production scheduler would pass this sweep. Add that sentence to declared_substitutions and the measurement stands.

referred_judgements.ruling: SPLIT. Enough for one, not for the other.

load_run_P9_body_sha256.ruling: DECLARING IS NOT ENOUGH. Must be measured.
load_run_P9_body_sha256.why: The measurement is unblocked today and its sibling proves it: decoupling computes body_sha256 itself (hash.digest('hex') over drained trace records) using only traceStart/traceDrain/reset — all live, no absent harness method, no attested hardware. load-run's own why_not_here concedes it: 'The hash comparison needs no attested hardware.' An owner of 'tool round 4' on work that is already unblocked is a deferral, not a debt. It is a small delta on a path that already ships in this repo.
